topic.title: Selection of internal project proposals for the annual innovation fund
topic.context: Five reviewers from different divisions of a mid-sized manufacturing company meet to allocate this year's internal innovation fund. Exactly one employee-submitted proposal will be carried forward.

options.label: A
options.name: Workflow Assistant
options.summary: A shared internal tool that reads team task boards and drafts status summaries, meeting agendas, and handover notes for circulation across the participating departments.

options.label: B
options.name: Supplier Data Hub
options.summary: A central repository that consolidates supplier records now kept separately by each business unit into one searchable catalog with shared update and review procedures.

options.label: C
options.name: Field Service App
options.summary: A mobile application for technicians visiting customer sites, covering job checklists, parts lookup, photo capture, and synchronization of records collected away from the network.

options.label: D
options.name: Training Studio
options.summary: An in-house production unit that develops short video and simulation modules for onboarding, refresher training, and the transfer of specialist skills between departments.

problems.1: Each year the fund gets committed before anyone asks which pocket the money will actually come out of, and that answer changes what is affordable. What worries me more is that the real bill often arrives with next year's renewal notice.
problems.2: It bothers me how confidently we promise delivery dates for work resting on conditions nobody here controls, from access at other companies' premises to whose hands are free when building starts. Twice now the technical groundwork turned out to be the part no one had checked beforehand.
problems.3: We have funded enough of these by now that a pattern ought to be visible, yet nobody opens the file on what became of earlier winners. What concerns me is that we keep rediscovering the same lesson about which kinds of work survive their first year.
problems.4: The thing I keep running into is that we judge these things by how impressive they sound rather than by what actually goes wrong on the floor each week. Nobody has put the everyday losses beside the everyday effort and looked at both.
problems.5: Nobody in this room has to name the people who will absorb the extra work, so we only find out when a rota breaks. It seems to me we treat staff time as if it were free and unlimited.

topic.title: Award of a national grant for basic research in the life sciences
topic.context: A five-member review panel convened by a national funding agency deliberates over the proposals that reached the final round. One multi-year grant is awarded in this cycle.

options.label: A
options.name: Microbiome Atlas
options.summary: A project cataloging microbial communities in soil samples collected across several climate zones and publishing the resulting sequences together with standardized site metadata.

options.label: B
options.name: Protein Folding Dynamics
options.summary: A study of how selected membrane proteins change shape over time, combining laboratory spectroscopy with simulation in order to describe intermediate structural states.

options.label: C
options.name: Regeneration in Amphibians
options.summary: An investigation of limb regrowth in salamander species, tracking cell populations and signaling activity through the successive stages of tissue restoration.

options.label: D
options.name: Plant Drought Signaling
options.summary: Research into the molecular signals that crops use to detect water shortage, conducted through controlled greenhouse trials across several cultivars and soil conditions.

problems.1: Every cycle the headline award looks the same size, yet what it actually buys keeps shrinking in some places and holding steady in others. Before ranking anything, I want to know which kinds of spending the agency still absorbs centrally and which now land on the awardee.
problems.2: Too many recent awards lost time to things that had nothing to do with the science itself, and the panel usually hears about it only after the money is committed. It seemed worth asking in advance where work in this field actually gets interrupted.
problems.3: Our judgements about promise have not aged well, and some of us have watched confident picks quietly stall while plainer ones kept earning their keep. Rather than trust that instinct once more, I went back through what finished awards here actually delivered and when.
problems.4: Nothing funded here runs in isolation, since it lands on shared facilities and services that no single award pays to expand. Given how often that spare capacity has been the thing that gives way, I looked at what state those services are in right now.
problems.5: Money can be voted through in an afternoon, while the trained hands a project needs take years to gather and can disappear in a season. That worry sent me to the question of who is genuinely available around here now, and who has already gone.

topic.title: Selection of a seed-stage company for a venture fund's next investment
topic.context: Five partners at an early-stage venture fund review the companies that cleared the final screening round. One company will receive this quarter's seed investment.

options.label: A
options.name: Ledger Bridge
options.summary: A company building software that reconciles payment records between small merchants and their banks, presenting matched and unmatched transactions together in a single dashboard.

options.label: B
options.name: Harvest Sensor
options.summary: A company developing in-field sensors and an accompanying service that reports soil and canopy conditions to growers on a seasonal subscription basis.

options.label: C
options.name: Clinic Scheduler
options.summary: A company offering appointment and staffing software for independent medical clinics, including reminders, waiting-list handling, and operational reporting for practice owners.

options.label: D
options.name: Fabric Loop
options.summary: A company operating a collection and resale channel for used apparel, running sorting facilities and an online storefront on behalf of participating clothing brands.

problems.1: Money has been leaving this partnership faster than any plan allowed for, and each quarter seems to end with less room than it began with. Before this cheque goes out I want to know what the years after a first round demand of us, and what we can borrow against when they do.
problems.2: Nearly everything in the last two cohorts arrived late, and never for the reason written in the plan — something outside the team's own hands always sat between the money going in and a first customer switching anything on. I would rather know now which kind of obstacle we are signing ourselves up for.
problems.3: The stories we tell about our wins have drifted a long way from what the returns actually came from. I keep wanting to walk back through everything already funded and see which of it kept its customers and which quietly did not.
problems.4: Our own quarter-end has become the worst fortnight of every three months, and much of it goes on numbers nobody here can check independently. Before adding to the book I want a clear view of what a new holding does to the way we close and report.
problems.5: Every company we back ends up asking us for people, and lately the asking takes more of the week than the deciding does. I want a straight look at who can actually be found right now and whose time here is left to give.

topic.title: Choice of a campus facility improvement plan for the coming fiscal year
topic.context: A five-member university committee of faculty and administrative staff reviews the facility plans submitted by departments. One plan will be carried out with next year's capital budget.

options.label: A
options.name: Central Study Commons
options.summary: A conversion of an underused ground-floor hall into open study space, with bookable group rooms, distributed power outlets, and a service desk near the entrance.

options.label: B
options.name: Laboratory Ventilation Upgrade
options.summary: A replacement of ventilation and fume extraction equipment throughout the shared teaching laboratories, together with revised layouts for the bench, storage, and preparation areas.

options.label: C
options.name: Campus Path Network
options.summary: A reworking of the walkways between the main buildings, covering lighting, surface renewal, sheltered sections, and wayfinding signage for visitors and new students.

options.label: D
options.name: Media Production Center
options.summary: A fitted-out suite of recording and editing rooms for course video, student projects, and public lectures, managed through a booking system open to campus users.

problems.1: The figures approved on paper no longer survive contact with the market, and what a building costs after it opens never reaches the committee at all.
problems.2: Every recent job seems to meet something nobody priced for, and the calendar keeps slipping until a year of building is squeezed into whatever weeks are left.
problems.3: Looking back at what has actually been built here, nobody has asked in the open which of those projects landed well and which quietly disappointed the people using them.
problems.4: Some of us keep noticing that space decisions are settled without asking what the timetable absorbs while the work runs, or how heavily the finished rooms get used afterwards.
problems.5: Each decision here lands on the same shrinking set of staff, and those already carrying the routine upkeep have had no relief for years.

topic.title: Selection of a redevelopment plan for a central municipal park
topic.context: A five-person review panel appointed by a city government examines the redevelopment plans prepared for a central park. One plan will be recommended to the council.

options.label: A
options.name: Wetland Restoration
options.summary: A plan that reshapes the park's drainage into a series of ponds and reed beds, with boardwalks and observation points arranged along the water's edge.

options.label: B
options.name: Sports Terraces
options.summary: A plan that replaces the open lawn with multi-use courts, a marked running loop, changing facilities, and stepped seating along the southern side of the site.

options.label: C
options.name: Market Plaza
options.summary: A plan that creates a paved central square with stall infrastructure, shade structures, and utility connections intended for weekend markets and seasonal events.

options.label: D
options.name: Woodland Walk
options.summary: A plan that plants dense tree cover across the northern half of the site, threaded with gravel paths, small clearings, and a visitor shelter near the main gate.

problems.1: Every scheme signed off here has looked affordable on the day and heavy on the accounts three years later. Sitting with the finance papers, I keep asking what this place will cost the city to keep once the ribbon is cut.
problems.2: Delivery dates in this city have a way of drifting once the diggers arrive, and the ground here has surprised us before. Before anyone commits, I want to know what this site and the handful of firms willing to work here will really let us finish.
problems.3: Something in how this city commissions work keeps producing handsome openings and short lives. I would rather judge by what the last decade of our schemes looks like now than by drawings.
problems.4: This park is not an empty stage; it is crossed, drained, mown and rained on every week of the year. What worries me is that we pick something which reads well on paper and then fights the way the ground and the people here actually behave.
problems.5: Every new thing the city opens lands on the same rota, and that rota is shorter each year. I am trying to work out who would really run and look after this place, week in and week out.

topic.title: Selection of a service expansion proposal for a public library system
topic.context: Five reviewers drawn from library staff and the community board deliberate over proposals for expanding services. One proposal will be implemented across the branch network.

options.label: A
options.name: Mobile Branch Service
options.summary: A vehicle-based lending service that visits outlying neighborhoods on a fixed weekly schedule, carrying a rotating collection and a staffed help desk at each stop.

options.label: B
options.name: Digital Archive Portal
options.summary: A program to scan local newspapers, photographs, and municipal records and publish them through a searchable portal with browsing and citation tools for researchers.

options.label: C
options.name: Maker Workshop
options.summary: A dedicated room in the main branch offering tools, materials, and scheduled instruction sessions for residents working on craft, repair, and electronics projects.

options.label: D
options.name: Language Learning Circles
options.summary: A recurring program of conversation groups and tutoring sessions in several languages, coordinated with trained facilitators and partner community organizations across the district.

problems.1: Every budget cycle looks sufficient on the day of the vote and thin by the second year, and the trouble seems to lie in how the funding is shaped rather than in its size.
problems.2: Too much of what we have started here depended on conditions we do not control, and the last few timetables came apart in the months when those conditions turned against us.
problems.3: It bothers me that we keep judging new ideas by how they sound in the room, when shapes very like them have already been tried in this system and left records nobody reopens.
problems.4: What keeps nagging at me is the knock-on: where our buildings sit and when they open already decides who can reach us, and every new commitment quietly reshuffles that.
problems.5: Staff absorb every new commitment on top of what they already do, and nobody checks beforehand whether the skills it needs are actually sitting on the roster.

topic.title: Selection of a care program for a regional hospital's development budget
topic.context: A five-member review panel of clinicians and hospital administrators considers the program proposals submitted by departments. One program will be established with this year's development budget.

options.label: A
options.name: Home Follow-Up Team
options.summary: A program in which nurses visit discharged patients at home for a defined period, recording recovery progress and coordinating each case with the treating department.

options.label: B
options.name: Day Rehabilitation Unit
options.summary: A program providing scheduled outpatient physical therapy in a dedicated space, equipped and staffed for both group sessions and individual treatment plans.

options.label: C
options.name: Chronic Care Coordination
options.summary: A program assigning coordinators to patients living with several long-term conditions, consolidating appointments, medication reviews, and communication with providers outside the hospital.

options.label: D
options.name: Perinatal Support Service
options.summary: A program offering scheduled consultations, classes, and follow-up contact for expectant and new parents, delivered jointly by the midwifery and pediatric departments.

problems.1: Every year the development money is voted through as though it were the whole cost, and the running side turns up unfunded twelve months later. Before anything is committed I would like to know what this budget can actually build and what any of it would earn back.
problems.2: Approval has never been the hard part here; things break in the second year, once the arrangement turns out to rest on a department or an outside body that never really signed up to it. I went looking for where our recent starts came apart.
problems.3: We have started and quietly buried enough initiatives that nobody can now say which of them ever changed anything for a patient. It seemed worth reading what the earlier attempts actually produced before we add another to the pile.
problems.4: Anything new has to fit into a day that is already full — the rooms, the approach roads, the booking screens everything must pass through. What worries me is less the merit of the idea than whether this place could absorb it without seizing up.
problems.5: Rosters are where every new program eventually lands, and the teams it lands on are rarely the ones that asked for it. Pressure sits so differently between one clinical group and the next that I wanted the staffing records in front of me.

topic.title: Selection of a transit improvement plan for a metropolitan authority
topic.context: Five reviewers appointed by a metropolitan transit authority deliberate over the improvement plans prepared for the network. One plan will be forwarded to the board.

options.label: A
options.name: Crosstown Bus Corridor
options.summary: A plan introducing a limited-stop bus route across the city's midsection, with dedicated lanes on selected segments and rebuilt boarding islands at the busiest stops.

options.label: B
options.name: Station Access Upgrades
options.summary: A plan reworking entrances, stairs, elevators, and passageways at a set of older stations to change how passengers move between the platforms and street level.

options.label: C
options.name: Integrated Fare Platform
options.summary: A plan replacing the current ticketing arrangements with a single account-based fare system covering the bus, rail, and regional ferry services together.

options.label: D
options.name: Night Service Extension
options.summary: A plan extending operating hours on the core routes into the late night, with adjusted staffing rosters, revised maintenance windows, and rewritten timetables.

problems.1: Every budget round lately turns into an argument over which pot the money may come from rather than what the network needs. Headline totals stopped meaning much to me once I saw what they commit us to paying in the years afterwards.
problems.2: Ever since the reorganisation, the schemes that stall are never the ones we expected to stall, and the cause is never anything written in the drawings. Before believing any delivery date now, I want to know who else has to say yes and what the ground might hide.
problems.3: Institutional memory here is short: the same ideas come back every decade and nobody looks up what happened last time. What I have started doing is reading the closure reports before the enthusiasm sets in.
problems.4: Complaints arrive about crowding, but when someone actually stands with a stopwatch the story often turns out different. What worries me is that we keep fixing whichever part of the trip gets talked about most rather than the part that costs passengers time.
problems.5: Plans here are written as if the people to run them will simply appear, and the same handful of crews end up carrying whatever we decide. Before anything is promised, I would rather know which rosters already have nothing left in them.

topic.title: Selection of a vendor for an enterprise resource planning replacement
topic.context: A five-person procurement review panel at a logistics company evaluates the shortlisted vendors for replacing its enterprise resource planning system. One vendor will be contracted.

options.label: A
options.name: Meridian Systems
options.summary: A vendor offering a hosted suite covering finance, inventory, and transport planning, delivered through a fixed configuration process and supported by a regional service team.

options.label: B
options.name: Corvus Platform
options.summary: A vendor providing a modular system assembled from separate finance, warehouse, and fleet components, each licensed and configured independently of the others.

options.label: C
options.name: Anchor Industrial Software
options.summary: A vendor supplying a system built specifically for transport operators, deployed on the company's own servers with an engineering team present through rollout.

options.label: D
options.name: Tessera Cloud Suite
options.summary: A vendor offering a subscription platform with configurable workflows and an application marketplace, with a partner firm handling data migration and staff training.

problems.1: Money here gets approved in one shape and refused in another, and a headline price has stopped telling me what a system will really cost us over its life. What worries me is the part of the bill that keeps arriving after everyone has stopped watching.
problems.2: Every project we run seems to founder on the same two things: nobody is quite in charge when something breaks, and the plan agreed at the start stops matching the business within months. I would rather know now which of those we are walking into again.
problems.3: Looking back at what this company has already lived through, two patterns bother me: systems that quietly age in place, and work handed outside that comes back needing repair.
problems.4: The part that keeps me awake is the depot floor: freight moves whether or not the office is mid-project, and the equipment out there is nobody's idea of modern. Anything we bring in has to survive our calendar and our yards as they actually are.
problems.5: We are thinner on people than the plan admits, and the ones who hold everything together are either leaving or already stretched across two roles. How a change lands on them, and on the crews who have to be retaught, weighs more with me than any feature list.

topic.context: Five members of a museum's exhibition committee review the proposals submitted by curators and partner institutions. One exhibition will occupy the main gallery next season.

options.label: A

options.summary: An exhibition tracing historical shipping routes through charts, cargo objects, and ship models, drawing on the museum's holdings alongside loans from partner maritime collections.

options.label: B

options.summary: An exhibition of locally produced weaving and dyeing, presenting garments and tools alongside recorded interviews and demonstration sessions with practicing craftspeople.

options.summary: An exhibition of kinetic and light-based artworks installed across the gallery, arranged in darkened zones with overhead rigging and works supplied by artist studios.

options.summary: An exhibition of finds from recent municipal digs, shown with reconstructions, site photography, and a working conservation bench visible to visitors from the walkway.

problems.1: Every season the money seems to end up somewhere other than the walls, and we only find out once the invoices land. Before another budget is set I would rather know which parts of a season quietly swallow it.
problems.2: Delivery is where this committee keeps getting caught out, approving something in good faith and then spending the season apologising at the door. I want to know where past seasons actually came unstuck, not where they were meant to.
problems.3: Looking back over the seasons I have sat through, the shows we were proudest of on paper are not the ones people came back for. Before the main room is committed again, the record should get a hearing first.
problems.4: The main room has to go on working as a building and not only as a display, and every season something arrives that the floor or the diary cannot absorb. I would rather learn that before the space is promised to anyone.
problems.5: We keep planning seasons as though the staff list were still what it was five years ago, when those left are carrying two roles each. What I want settled is who would actually do the work and who would be standing in the room.
